claims.wording: Schwab International is probably unavailable (Albania is not on its reported list)

sources.name: Your Tax Base: Charles Schwab for expats
sources.says: Published October 23, 2026. On that day the author ran every entry in Schwab's international account selector through the application: it accepted residents of 51 of 263 countries and regions: Argentina, Australia, Austria, the Bahamas, Belgium, Bermuda, Brazil, the British Virgin Islands, the Cayman Islands, Chile, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, Finland, Germany, Greece, Guatemala, Hong Kong, Iceland, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Jersey, Luxembourg, Malaysia, the Marshall Islands, Mexico, the Netherlands, Norway, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and Uruguay. Named as not accepted: Canada, Croatia, the Dominican Republic, France, Italy, Japan, Malta, New Zealand, the Philippines, South Africa, Turkey and Vietnam; for the rest the application said "Schwab currently cannot open accounts for residents of your country/region." The test covers new applicants on that day only.

sources.name: Your Tax Base: Charles Schwab for expats
sources.says: Dated October 23, 2026 (country check that day). The United Arab Emirates is on the 51-country accepted list and marked "Yes"; South Africa is marked "No" (the 12 "No" rows: Canada, Croatia, Dominican Republic, France, Italy, Japan, Malta, New Zealand, Philippines, South Africa, Turkey, Vietnam). Montenegro, Albania and Mauritius are in neither list; the article says 200 of the 263 countries and regions in Schwab's selector showed that Schwab "currently cannot open accounts for residents of your country/region". It quotes the Schwab One International terms: "Customers residing within Europe are restricted from using their Available Margin Loan Value to withdraw funds from their account."

claims.note: Albania is in neither the accepted 51 nor the 12 marked "No". Lending score stays 3 ("IBKR only"), and would stay 3 under the London/Zurich reading of Schwab's "residing within Europe" clause even if Schwab accepted Albanians, since Albania is in Europe.

claims.claim: US citizens can stay up to a year visa-free, with more than 90 days outside Albania before a new year

sources.name: Himara.net: Albania visa requirements 2026
sources.says: Dated 22 February 2026 (it cites a joint ministerial instruction no. 91 of 30 April 2026, which is later than that date). US passport holders enter visa-free for "up to one year (365 days)"; border checks apply "90 days in 180, or one year for citizens of the United States of America"; after the year, US citizens must leave for 90 days before re-entering.

sources.name: Exit News: Albania restores one-year stay for US citizens
sources.says: Dated 4 March 2022. US citizens "can re-enter and stay without a residence permit" for "a new term of up to one year" "if they have stayed outside the territory of the Republic of Albania for more than 90 days"; decided "in support of the law "On Foreigners"".

sources.name: Law No. 79/2021 on foreigners, consolidated with Law 43/2025 (Agency for Foreigners and Migration, asp.gov.al)
sources.says: Consolidated text "i përditësuar" with Law 43/2025 of 26.6.2025. Article 85: foreigners "që janë në pension në vendin e tyre" (retired in their own country) may apply for a residence permit for pensioners; it is renewable every year if the criteria set by Council of Ministers decision are still met; it is a permit "dhënë në bazë të pensionit jashtë vendit" (granted on a pension from abroad) and allows no economic activity. Article 84: a temporary permit for owners of real estate, up to 1 year at first and renewable yearly, criteria by Council of Ministers decision; no value is set in the law. Article 31(2): short stays are limited to 90 days in 180 "except where otherwise provided".

claims.note: The law's Article 31(2) limits short stays to 90 in 180 days "except where otherwise provided"; the one-year rule for US citizens is set by government decision. Two dated secondary pages (2026 and 2022) give it; al.usembassy.gov returned HTTP 403 and travel.state.gov was not tried (403 in earlier stages).
